item.description:
brndnmtthws/conky | 8550 stars| 673 forks.

| CMake | Python | Lua | C | C++ | Shell | Dockerfile | Objective-C++ | JavaScript | TypeScript |

Light-weight system monitor for X, Wayland, and other things, too

Conky v1.26.0

Conky v1.26.0 adds ${pa_source_volume} for the default PulseAudio recording source, fixes silent truncation of long ${exec} commands and merging of threaded and blocking exec callbacks, handles X11 desktop name lists without a final NUL, and loads bundled Lua bindings correctly in AppImages.

Full Changelog: v1.25.5...v1.26.0

Highlights Since v1.25.5

Audio

  • Add ${pa_source_volume} for the default PulseAudio recording source (#2519). It reports the configured source volume averaged across channels, preserves values above 100% when amplification is enabled, ignores mute state, and refreshes when the server's default source changes. Source-only servers without a playback sink are also supported.

Execution

  • Long ${exec} commands are no longer silently truncated: the shared 256-byte command buffer has been replaced with owned, dynamically sized storage, and the out-of-bounds terminator write at exactly 256 bytes is fixed (#2520). text_buffer_size still controls configuration parsing.
  • Threaded (${texeci}, ${texecpi}) and blocking (${exec}, ${execi}, and related) callbacks for the same command are now tracked separately, so their wait policies can no longer be merged (#2517). Same-mode deduplication and interval merging are preserved.

X11

  • Parse the final desktop name even when the X11 desktop-name list lacks a trailing NUL, as some window managers such as bspwm provide, so ${desktop_name} is reported correctly (#2518).

Packaging

  • AppImage Lua bindings now resolve at runtime: when APPDIR is set, $APPDIR/usr/lib/conky/lib?.so is prepended to Lua's package.cpath while existing fallbacks remain (#2513). AppImage packaging also includes a PNG icon for .DirIcon.

    loader from following stale symbol version definitions and crashing before

item.title: [meta/flow] v0.338.0
item.description:
meta/flow | 22304 stars| 1892 forks.

| Shell | JavaScript | Makefile | Ruby | CSS | Vim Snippet | TypeScript | Rust | RenderScript | MDX |

Adds static typing to JavaScript to improve developer productivity and code quality.

Breaking Changes:

  • Flowconfig option experimental.assertion_functions is removed. Assertion functions have been on by default and the option only accepted true since 0.337.
  • Flowconfig option experimental.disable_invariant_special_casing is removed. It has been on by default and only accepted true since 0.337.
  • Flowconfig option experimental.function_and_object_type_is_no_longer_any is removed. It has been on by default and only accepted true for a while.
  • Flowconfig option experimental.builtin_ts_libdef_dynamic_discovery is removed. It has been on by default and only accepted true.
  • Flowconfig option experimental.declare_global_support is removed. It has been on by default and only accepted true.

Likely to cause new Flow errors:

  • Readonly, Partial, Required, $Exact, Omit and mapped types over an interface now include its methods and the members it inherits.
  • Type guards now refine Array<any>, {data: any}, Map<string, any> and similar types to the guarded type, e.g. Array<string>, which can surface errors in code that relied on any.
  • Static members can no longer reference the type parameters of their class, like in TypeScript, and reading a static member of a generic class no longer infers them.
  • keyof of an object with a template literal indexer no longer widens the indexer key to string in conditional types like Exclude.

New Features:

  • Mapped types over arrays and tuples support readonly and writeonly modifiers.
  • Property truthiness checks such as if (result.done) now refine unions of classes and interfaces by fields with literal types, as === checks already did.
  • Type guards narrow through optional calls such as isString?.(x). When the callee or receiver is nullable, only the true branch narrows.
  • Support optional assertion calls when their declared types guarantee the call runs.
  • Added the intrinsic ExactObjectType, the supertype of every exact object type and a subtype of {...}.

Notable bug fixes:

  • Fix crashes and false recursive-definition errors from cyclic type star exports in TypeScript declarations.
  • Support namespace export aliases and ambient exported members in TypeScript definitions.
  • Allow classes to extend a constructor whose overloads are not all generic, such as Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>.
  • Casting a value whose type intersects an enum with other types (e.g. E & E) to the enum's representation type no longer errors.
  • Arrays can be assigned to variables and parameters whose type was inferred from new Array<T>(...).
  • Report delegated yield type errors at the yield expression.
  • Align Try Flow's default lints and declare global support with regular Flow.
  • Improve inference for generic values passed to polymorphic operations.
  • Fix Try Flow initialization after the async builtin migration while preserving older releases' library definitions.
  • Report conditional type instantiation errors at the caller.
  • Apply type-parameter defaults when omitted optional or nullable arguments are the only evidence for them.
  • An object with an indexer is no longer checked against optional properties it doesn't declare of a TypeScript-declared (.d.ts) object type, matching TypeScript.
  • Fewer underconstrained-implicit-instantiation errors for generic calls passed as arguments to other generic calls.
  • Fixed a crash when printing long types that contain non-ASCII names in error messages.
  • Tuple types with a spread keep the variance of their own elements, e.g. a in [readonly a: unknown, ...T] stays read-only.
  • First in [infer First, ...infer Rest] is now inferred instead of unknown.
  • Fixed a deadlock in the Flow server monitor that could make all subsequent commands fail with "Out of retries, exiting!".
  • Type guards with a union type now refine union members precisely, e.g. a falsy-value guard on string | number refines to "" | 0.
  • Type guards now drop union members that are instances of classes unrelated to the guarded class, e.g. x: A | B refined by x is A is now A rather than A | (A & B).
  • The negative branch of a type guard now refines away generics that satisfy the guard, e.g. x: T | number refined by !isT(x) with isT: (x: unknown) => x is T is now number.
  • In the negative branch of a type guard, any now stays any instead of becoming empty, and boolean is refined to the literal the guard does not cover.
  • Correct stdin behavior for flow check-contents and flow autocomplete.
  • Error messages print code that contains backticks, such as template literals, as markdown code spans.
  • Instances of TypeScript-declared generics, such as React.MouseEvent<T>, now compare type parameters without a variance annotation covariantly, as type applications already did.
  • Type guards now drop tuple members of a different length and array members with disjoint element types.
  • Type guards now drop object and interface union members whose properties conflict with the guard type.
  • x instanceof C no longer refines a value of an intersection type to empty.
  • Linux release builds use jemalloc, which keeps the memory of long-running servers from growing after large rechecks.
  • Fixed a race that could leave a file unmerged after a recheck, which made the server recheck forever while an open file imported it.

Misc:

  • Print rest arrays as array types in errors.
  • Print receiver and merged declaration types in errors.
  • Simplify missing this annotation diagnostics.
  • Print both types in inheritance errors.
  • Identify missing parameter annotations directly at the parameter location.
  • Remove empty filename metadata from the Try Flow AST display.
  • Add a default-on option to hide locations in the Try Flow AST pane.
  • Show node types first in the Try Flow AST pane.
  • Add a default-on option to hide null and undefined fields in the Try Flow AST pane.
  • Move Try Flow's JSON error output into an Errors format pill bar.
  • Add JSON AST output to Try Flow.

Parser:

  • Accept explicit semicolons on shorthand ambient modules.
  • Accept keyword members in qualified type names and import types.
  • Allow repeated inline interface exports in TypeScript files.
  • Fixed flow-parser taking minutes to parse JS files over ~1 MB.
  • Support destructured rest parameters in function type signatures.
  • Support import attributes on re-export declarations.
  • Preserve TypeScript accessibility modifiers on bodyless class method signatures.
  • Preserve computed type-literal keys as properties in TypeScript source files.
  • Allow newline-separated type members in TypeScript source files.
  • Use "in out" for the ESTree variance kind of in out type parameters.
  • Parse postfix non-null assertions with type syntax enabled, preserve ASI, and emit TypeScript-compatible NonNullExpression nodes.
  • Respect JavaScript line terminators and Unicode whitespace when recovering source locations.
  • Parse default interface exports and report unsupported syntax during type checking.
  • Correct inferred ESTree source type for default interfaces, inline type specifiers, and exported import aliases.
  • Exclude default interface exports and all-type specifier lists from inferred Babel module source type.
  • Support top-level await for explicit modules and .mjs/.mts files in flow-parser.
  • Always enable type parsing for TypeScript filenames.
  • Reject type syntax in untyped parser mode and report precise diagnostics.
  • Fix declaration method signature locations to include the complete signature.
  • Include the const keyword in const enum declaration locations.

IDE:

  • Hover and error messages no longer print redundant parentheses around function types in maybe types, e.g. ?() => void instead of ?(() => void).

Library Definitions:

  • Align well-known symbol members (Symbol.toStringTag, Symbol.match, Symbol.toPrimitive, ...) with TypeScript.
  • Map and WeakMap set, and Set and WeakSet add, now return this.
  • RegExp flags/sticky/unicode and Number.EPSILON/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER/MIN_SAFE_INTEGER are now read-only; String.prototype.normalize accepts the normalization form literals and the legacy HTML methods (bold, link, ...) are declared.
  • Array.prototype.copyWithin returns this, so subclasses of Array keep their type.
  • Array.prototype.sort returns this, so subclasses of Array keep their type.
  • Math constants (Math.PI, Math.E, ...) are read-only.
  • Number.MAX_VALUE, MIN_VALUE, NaN, NEGATIVE_INFINITY and POSITIVE_INFINITY are read-only.
  • String#split requires a separator, String#replace has separate overloads for a string and a function replacement, and String#length is read-only, as in TypeScript.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2018 async iterator and iterable definitions.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2018 async generator definitions.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2019 array definitions while preserving Flow's existing flatMap union order and inference.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2020 promise definitions, including mutable settled results.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2016 array includes definitions while keeping Flow's element refinement.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2015 generator definitions. Generator.prototype.return now requires a value of the generator's return type.
  • Add React.CSSProperties, typed by csstype.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2015 promise definitions, adapted to Flow's inference.
  • Use TypeScript's ESNext set method definitions, including Set.prototype.union.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2015 Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet definitions. size is now read-only.
  • done is now optional in the non-final branch of IteratorResult, as in TypeScript.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2015 iterable definitions. ArrayIterator, MapIterator, SetIterator and StringIterator are now interfaces, and StringIterator takes a type argument.
  • Add React's DOM types from @types/react, such as React.MouseEvent, React.HTMLAttributes and React.JSX.IntrinsicElements.
  • React.ComponentProps of a string that is not a JSX intrinsic is empty in roots that define their own $JSXIntrinsics.
  • Use TypeScript's ESNext iterator helper definitions. reduce without an initial value now requires the reducer to return the iterator's element type.
  • Array, ReadonlyArray and typed array toLocaleString now accept locales and formatting options.
  • Use TypeScript's ES2015 core definitions.

    invalid Region reaches the rules instead of panicking with invalid params. Requests still run the validators.

Service Features:

  • aws-sdk-amp (1.129.0): Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and CloudWatch.
  • aws-sdk-bedrockagentruntime (1.151.0): Adds the CodeExecution step and codeExecution action to AgenticRetrieveStream trace events, showing when the agent runs code and which documents it reads.
  • aws-sdk-cloudwatchlogs (1.162.0): Adds support for account-level retention policies in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Customers can now use PutAccountPolicy with the new RETENTION POLICY type to set default log retention across all log groups in an account. Includes dry-run mode to preview the impact of policy changes before applying them.
  • aws-sdk-connect (1.220.0): Amazon Connect adds tag-based access control for Contact Lens rules. ListRealtimeContactAnalysisSegmentsV2 adds a ListFilter to return only category segments whose rules match given tags. PreEvaluationFilter now supports contact evaluation resources for OnContactEvaluationSubmit rules.
  • aws-sdk-customerprofiles (1.136.0): Adds support for template ingestion controls in the GetProfileObjectTypeTemplate API response.
  • aws-sdk-docdb (1.128.0): Amazon DocumentDB now returns ServerlessV2PlatformVersion in DBCluster API responses and adds the DescribeServerlessV2PlatformVersions API to discover available platform versions and their capabilities.
  • aws-sdk-lambda (1.156.0): Adds ConsumptionMode to SelfManagedKafkaEventSourceConfig, letting Lambda event source mappings consume self-managed Apache Kafka topics as a queue. Set ConsumptionMode to Queue when creating an event source mapping.
  • aws-sdk-omics (1.137.0): Adds the outputUriPrefixMode parameter to StartRun and GetRun. You can now write run outputs directly under outputUri, without the prefixes the service adds by default. When you opt in, outputs overwrite existing objects at the same keys.
  • aws-sdk-sagemaker (1.248.0): Create endpoints with AcceleratorPartitionLayouts on ProductionVariant and deploy inference components with AcceleratorPartitionType in ComputeResourceRequirements to divide accelerators into hardware-isolated NVIDIA MIG partitions, running multiple models per GPU. P4d, P5, G7, G7e.
  • aws-sdk-timestreaminfluxdb (1.113.0): Add DeploymentConfiguration field to CreateDbCluster and UpdateDbCluster APIs to support creation of heterogenous InfluxDB v3 Enterprise clusters.

item.title: [semgrep/semgrep] Release v1.183.0
item.description:
semgrep/semgrep | 17379 stars| 1136 forks.

| Makefile | OCaml | Standard ML | Python | JavaScript | C | Java | Shell | Dockerfile | Go |

Lightweight static analysis for many languages. Find bug variants with patterns that look like source code.

1.183.0 - 2026-10-29

### Added

  • The --help output of semgrep subcommands now includes a "THIRD-PARTY
    LICENSES" section linking to the licenses and notices for Semgrep's open
    source dependencies at https://semgrep.dev/cli-credits. (cli-credits)
  • Pro: Supply Chain now records which Go module requires which when dependency paths are enabled and local builds are allowed, so transitive Go findings can show the dependency path. (SC-4268)

### Changed

  • Semgrep no longer ships binaries for Intel Macs; 1.182 is the last release that supports them. On Intel Macs, use the semgrep/semgrep Docker image; on Apple Silicon, use a native arm64 Python. (drop-intel-macos)

  • Speed up scans with many rules that share file prefilter conditions by checking each condition once per file. (prefilter-predicate-memo)

  • semgrep ci --no-suppress-errors now exits with code 2 (instead of 0) when dependency resolution fails for a subproject while local builds are allowed (--allow-local-builds): a build or package manager command fails, a lockfile cannot be parsed at all, or a build succeeds but reports an incomplete dependency list (for example, a registry refused a request). The affected dependency sources are listed in the scan output and the scan no longer reports that it completed successfully. Findings from the other subprojects are still reported. The default behavior, where errors are suppressed, is unchanged, and so is any scan without --allow-local-builds. Semgrep Managed Scanning scans are not affected. (SC-3613)

  • bash grammar update (v0.25.1):

    • Bash arithmetic ($(( )), $[ ], (( )), C-style for headers) is now translated into operator trees with bash precedence, so patterns such as $(( $X * 2 )) match structurally. $((...)) is no longer confused with $(...).
    • Bash patterns accept a lone ... before done, fi or }, e.g. while ...; do ... done, and until loops now parse as loops.
    • Bash words containing # (x=foo#bar) are no longer truncated, and arguments after a redirect or heredoc delimiter stay with their command.
    • Many Bash constructs that failed to parse now parse, e.g. $[ ], time ( ... ), extglob in case and [[ ]], and if function bodies.

    (bash-v0.25.1)

  • clojure grammar update (v0.0.13):

    • Clojure source parsing now accepts reader-evaluated metadata, such as ^#=(keyword "a") [1 2], including the legacy #^ prefix. Semgrep does not execute reader evaluation, and metadata remains ignored during matching.
    • Clojure source parsing now supports reader conditionals inside symbolic values, such as ## #?(:clj Inf :cljs NaN), retaining the conditional branches without evaluating them.

    (clojure-v0.0.13)

  • swift grammar update (0.5.0):

    • Swift parsing now supports type and value parameter packs, including each/repeat expansions and pack constraints.
    • Swift parsing now supports if and switch expressions used as variable initializers.
    • Swift parsing now supports macro declarations with typed signatures and #externalMacro definitions. This does not implement macro expansion.
    • Swift property observers now retain their willSet/didSet bodies and parameters separately from property initializers.
    • Swift parsing now supports borrowing, consuming, package, and distributed modifiers while preserving their distinct spellings.
    • Swift parsing now supports #unavailable conditions and distinguishes them from #available conditions. Both are mapped as #… expression nodes (not boolean Not) so patterns like if !$X do not match availability checks.
    • Swift parsing now supports member access on parenthesized existential types, such as (any P).self, and preserves the underlying parenthesized existential or opaque type.
    • Swift parsing now supports references to the bitwise AND operator using (&).

    (swift-0.5.0)

### Fixed

  • The Cursor hooks installed by semgrep mcp now track edited files separately for each Cursor conversation, so one window's stop scan no longer scans or discards another conversation's edits. (mcp-hook-cache-per-conversation)
  • The semgrep mcp server's semgrep_scan tool now only scans files inside the client's workspace root, or the server's working directory when the client reports none. Set SEMGREP_MCP_ALLOW_SCAN_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE=true to scan files outside it. (mcp-scan-workspace-roots)
  • Interfile scans no longer fail with Failure: Failed to unmarshal cached value: Exception during parallelization: Exception.Timeout(...) when a
    taint configuration timeout fires at an unlucky moment. The timeout now only
    skips the affected rule and file, as intended. (CODE-9810)
  • The Semgrep source distribution on PyPI is once again published with provenance. (CODE-10070)
  • Update certificate trust in Semgrep and its container images to address the eMudhra certificate authority compromise. Disable curl-based telemetry on macOS and Windows; default telemetry and scanning remain available. (INCID-521)
  • Supply Chain: multi-document pnpm-lock.yaml files (written by pnpm 11+) are
    now parsed instead of reporting zero dependencies. A lockfile that fails to
    parse now marks its subproject as unresolved rather than resolved with zero
    dependencies. (SC-3870)
  • Supply Chain now parses go.mod files that contain a godebug ( ... ) block. Such files used to report no dependencies and a parse error. (SC-4268)
  • Supply Chain now finds the direct dependencies of Poetry projects that declare them in the [project] dependencies table (Poetry 2.0 and later), in dependency groups or as extras, instead of reporting every package with unknown transitivity. Packages from Poetry dependency groups are now reported as direct. PyPI rule matching now ignores differences in case, -, _ and . in package names, so rules match however a lockfile spells the name. (SC-4278)
  • Supply Chain now parses yarn.lock files generated by yarn 0.16 and earlier, whose header has no blank line after # yarn lockfile v1. Previously these failed with "Failed to parse yarn.lock at 1:1" and no dependencies were analyzed. (SC-4286)
  • Recognize all valid Python f-string prefixes without accepting invalid prefix combinations. (gh-11913)

### Infra/Release Changes

  • Apply external rule-test expectations consistently in CLI and OCaml CI tests. (rule-expectation-ci)
  • Add --override-expectations to the OCaml rule test runner to replace expected finding lines for individual targets, rules, and engines from an external JSON file. (rule-test-expectations)

sbcl/sbcl | 2163 stars| 364 forks.

| Common Lisp | Shell | Makefile | C | Assembly | C++ | Emacs Lisp | Python |

Mirror of Steel Bank Common Lisp (SBCL)'s official repository
  • minor incompatible change: testing for float equality using = is now a
    quiet operation, not signalling when given NaNs as input.
  • enhancement: Unicode support has been updated to support version 18.0.0 of
    the Unicode standard, including support for new scripts and additional
    characters, refinements to segmentation algorithms and a number of fixes
    for bugs uncovered along the way:
    ** minor incompatible change: SB-UNICODE:LINE-BREAK-CLASS no longer
    accepts a :RESOLVE keyword argument.
    ** enhancement: the implementation of line-breaking rules for numbers now
    implements the full number-like state machine rather than the previous
    table-based approximation.
    ** enhancement: UTS10-style collation through SB-UNICODE:UNICODE< and
    similar functions now supports the use of #\uFFFE as a field separator
    and #\uFFFF as an upper bound.
    ** bug fix: the set of characters considered of type Close for sentence
    breaking no longer includes Other Punctuation.
    ** bug fix: in sentence breaking, do not attach a CR not followed by a LF
    to its preceding character for the purpose of cluster class
    determination.
    ** bug fix: some characters corresponding to unallocated code points in
    Hangul blocks are no longer treated as having Hangul syllable type T.
    ** bug fix: Ahom vowel sounds A and AA are no longer treated as being of
    class Spacing Break Mark in grapheme clustering.
    ** bug fix: character corresponding to surrogate code points are no longer
    treated as Control grapheme-break class.
    ** bug fix: emoji extenders are now in the Extend sentence-break class.
    ** bug fix: Complex Context-Dependent characters are handled as Alphabetic
    or Combining Marks according to the default resolution in Unicode
    line-breaking.
    ** bug fix: combining marks attached to otherwise unattached zero-width
    joiners no longer inhibit line breaks.
  • bug fix: subnormal floating point numbers print with the least number of
    digits required to discriminate between adjacent floats, just as normal
    floating point numbers do. (thanks to Arthur Miller)
  • bug fix: inconsistency and heap corruption in :weakness :key hash tables
    in some circumstances. (lp#2169495, reported by Igor Santos)
  • bug fix: miscompilation of DPB and (SETF LDB) causing the wrong bit to be
    set in some circumstances. (lp#2168668, reported by Willem Broekema)
  • bug fix: compiler crash from parsing REAL types with large integer bounds.
    (lp#2168680)
  • bug fix: fix miscompilation involving constants of size between 64 and
    128 bits on backends with a register pair implementation. (lp#2168763,
    #lp#2168767)
  • bug fix: an infinite loop in the compiler's type solver. (lp#2168790)
  • bug fix: non-convergent behaviour in constraint propagation. (lp#2168862)
  • bug fix: SB-GMP could be caused to return malformed ratios. (lp#2168973,
    reported by David Scherfgen)
  • bug fix: SB-GMP returned the wrong value for GCD with an argument of the
    form -2^(64k-1). (lp#2168975, reported by David Scherfgen)
  • bug fix: better compiler reasoning for funcalling values derived as
    mixtures of non-function and function-types, in particular excluding NULL
    from being successfully funcalled. (lp#2168999, thanks to Vasily
    Postnicov)
  • bug fix: various compiler errors. (lp#2169379, lp#2171292, lp#2171329)
  • bug fix: emit a compiler warning when ARRAY-DIMENSION is called with an
    axis argument known to be out of bounds for its array argument.
    (lp#2169659, thanks to Vasily Postnicov)
  • bug fix: fix a test to actually test weak hash tables with EQL keys, which
    had been failing to test anything since 2006. (lp#2171410, reported by
    Igor Santos)
  • bug fix: some compiler notes about deleted code were silenced.
  • bug fix: in compiler messages, the outermost element of the processing
    path was always missing, and the actual source form also got corrupted
    sometimes.
  • bug fix: evaluator errors from the simple evaluator now inherit from
    PROGRAM-ERROR.
  • bug fix: some bug fixes to the mark-region garbage collector (thanks to
    iska and Hayley Patton)
  • bug fix: address bugs in the reader regarding float syntax with large
    (resp. small) decimal fraction and very large negative (resp. positive)
    exponent. (thanks to Arthur Miller)
  • bug fix: allow usage of SB-ASSEM:INST when *PRINT-CASE* is not :UPCASE.
    (thanks to digikar99)
  • bug fix: PRIN1-TO-STRING of MOST-NEGATIVE-FIXNUM failed with an internal
    error when PRINT-BASE was 2 or 4. (thanks to Arthur Miller)
  • bug fix: address a compiler failure related to MAKE-DOUBLE-FLOAT on PPC64.
    (thanks to Piotr Kubaj)
  • bug fix: types expressed as REAL and FLOAT ranges handle type conversion
    of their bounds more carefully.
  • bug fix: type checking for :KEY and :TEST arguments to ASSOC and RASSOC
    uses the right data. (reported by Tito Latini)
  • bug fix: miscompilation of conversions from (SIMPLE-ARRAY CHARACTER (*))
    to UTF-8. (reported by Tom Gillespie)
  • bug fix: a large number of issues found through extended random testing.
  • optimization: some calls to EQUALP with a constant array argument can be
    constant-folded if enough is known about the type of the other argument.
    (lp#2169625, thanks to Vasily Postnicov)
  • optimization: some type information was lost in (SAFETY 0) code leading
    to slower generated code. (reported by Qiantan Hong)
  • optimization: complete unboxed signed 128-bit arithmetic on arm64 and
    x86-64, except for division.
  • optimization: improved type derivation for local functions.
  • optimization: loops with iteration variables tested for termination by
    equality (rather than inequality) have better type inference.
  • optimization: the compiler's handling of constraints has been optimized to
    do less work somewhat faster.
  • optimization: provide support for a four-way 64-bit permutation
    instruction in SB-SIMD for AVX2. (thanks to Willem Broekema)
  • optimization: the compiler is more aware of the return type of LOG in the
    presence of mixed floating point formats.
  • documentation: SB-MANUAL has several new sections: @GETTING-SBCL,
    @RUNNING-WITHOUT-INSTALLATION, @PARTS-OF-SBCL, @FINDING-PARTS-OF-SBCL, and
    many more under @EFFICIENCY.
  • documentation: SB-MANUAL now includes variable initforms and argument
    default values in the Texinfo output.
  • documentation: provide an improved example of package-local nicknames.
    (reported by Jacek Podkanski)

item.title: [gperftools/gperftools] gperftools-2.19.2
item.description:
gperftools/gperftools | 8986 stars| 1539 forks.

| Shell | Makefile | C++ | C | Assembly | M4 | CMake | Ruby | Starlark |

Main gperftools repository

This is another quick bug-fix release on top of 2.19.1. It updates the vendored aw-backtrace.

Updated aw-backtrace expands x86-64 DRAP support. With -march=x86-64-v3 (e.g. Ubuntu 26.04's amd64v3 variant) gcc realigns the stack for AVX much more often, and a realigned function that also passes arguments on the stack uses a DRAP frame. The layout of those frames turned out to be more general than we previously assumed, so backtraces through them were truncated (this affected CPU and heap profiles as well as debugallocation's stack traces). This fixes the test failures seen on github's Ubuntu 26.04 builders.
